Original images are not bundled. Only approved selected examples are compressed and published; all other attempts remain audit records.

images.prompt: Natural product photograph of one plain dark desk tape dispenser on a wide off-white windowsill. A single translucent tape roll sits in the rear circular opening and a short tape strip runs toward the low front cutting edge. Soft daylight from the left, neutral wall, side three-quarter camera, entire dispenser visible. Vertical 4:5, 1024x1280. Full objects visible with breathing room. Natural photography, realistic materials and lighting; no text, logo, watermark, or illustration.

review.reason: Independently inspected one complete tape dispenser with one roll, visible dark spool, a single clear strip spanning the open trough, and a metal serrated cutter. The body and window context are coherent and unbranded.

images.actual_source_analysis: One dark charcoal desk tape dispenser rests on an off-white windowsill. Its tall rounded rear is at upper right and its low cutting end at front left. One translucent tape roll sits around a dark circular spool in the rear opening. A single clear tape strip bridges forward across the open trough to a narrow metal serrated cutting blade. The heavy elongated body and thin darker base rim are fully visible, and the central concavity remains open. A window occupies the upper left, with soft daylight from the left and a plain pale wall behind.

images.prompt:
Fine-aggregate cast terrazzo with a warm cement matrix, irregular stone chips, and matte ground surfaces.
Preserve: Subject count, outer silhouette, openings, attachments, and contact points. Source camera viewpoint, framing, relative scale, and placement. Recognizable subject identity and existing background structure.
Recast existing solid subject surfaces as fine-aggregate terrazzo, retaining openings, functional parts, silhouette, and source support contacts.
Use a warm ivory matrix with muted coral and charcoal chips; keep aggregate colors limited and balanced.
Preserve original edges and apertures exactly; do not create outlines or new seams.
Distribute irregular stone chips through the material at a plausible scale, with flat exposed cross-sections and subtle matrix pores.
Keep source lighting and use broad matte highlights with grounded shadows rather than glossy polished marble reflections.
Maintain the original object count, framing, perspective, placement, and proportions.
Wrap aggregate naturally over curved forms without repeating a flat wallpaper pattern or erasing fine geometry.
Finish with smoothly ground but matte surfaces and believable mass; avoid extra pedestals, ornaments, or embedded lettering.
Change existing solid surfaces and their material response only; retain parts, silhouettes, openings, and placement.
Use the supplied photograph as the sole composition reference. Keep the entire source frame, original 4:5 aspect ratio, camera viewpoint, subject scale, and all margins. Produce at least 1024x1280 pixels. Output only the finished image.
Avoid: Oversized gemstones, repeating wallpaper chips, or decorative mosaics. Filled openings, fused movable parts, changed silhouette, or extra pieces. Glossy marble veins, text, logos, watermarks, or inscriptions.

review.reason: Independent comparison confirms dispenser body, roll/spool separation, clear tape strip, open trough and fine cutter teeth remain intact. Fine irregular stone chips sit in a matte warm cement matrix without swallowing details or repeating as wallpaper. No fused mechanism, added pieces or decoration.
